title: Clean sign-up fields that users paste

blocks.text: The sign-up form saves names and addresses that users type, or paste from web pages, word processors and spreadsheets. The duplicate-customer report keeps finding pairs such as `Tomás` and a `Tomás` that looks identical, and support found accounts whose required last name is blank on screen but passed validation.
`SignupForm.accept(...)` already cleans every field and checks the required ones. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/SignupForm.java`:

items: `clean(value)`: the value without the blank-looking characters around it;
`missing(value)`: whether the value shows as nothing at all.

blocks.text: When you're done, a pasted value is saved the same as the typed one, and a required field that shows nothing is reported missing. About three lines in total.

cases.says: spaces, tabs and line breaks around a typed value are removed
a required field that is empty or only spaces is reported as missing, by name
an optional field of only spaces is saved as an empty value
no-break spaces around a value, as a web page pastes them, are removed too
wide Unicode spaces such as the ideographic space and the en space are removed
a required field holding only no-break spaces is missing, not filled in
only the space around a value goes; the spaces between its words stay as they were

origin.section: trim() Stops at U+0020, strip() at Unicode Whitespace, and Neither Removes a No-Break Space

concepts: trim() removes only characters up to U+0020, strip() and isBlank() use Character.isWhitespace, and neither removes the no-break space U+00A0.
